shortDescription: A balanced coir-based mix for general foliage plants with fibrous, terrestrial roots.
rationaleTemplate: A standard coir-based mix suits {species}: its terrestrial fibrous roots want even moisture with steady drainage, and the coir-perlite-bark balance gives container capacity around 65–80% without saturating the root zone.
citations: Gemini-report:Substrate Component Analysis and Transition to Peat-Free Media

shortDescription: Bark-dominant, fast-reaerating mix for hemi-epiphytic climbing aroids.

recipe.notes: Holds moisture and nutrients between waterings.
Permanent air pathways; pumice preferred for weight.
Adsorbs salts and keeps the mix fresh.

rationaleTemplate: A chunky aroid mix suits {species}: hemi-epiphytic climbers grow oxygen-hungry aerial roots that suffocate in peat-perlite blends, so a bark-led recipe with pumice and charcoal keeps air-filled porosity high and resists long-term compaction.

shortDescription: Mineral-led, low-fertility mix for water-storing succulents and xerophytes.

recipe.notes: Minimal organic component; just enough water-holding.

rationaleTemplate: A gritty, mineral-heavy mix suits {species}: water-storing tissues mean the plant draws on internal reserves between waterings, so the substrate must dry rapidly and never sit saturated — pumice plus coarse sand and a thin organic fraction delivers AFP in the 25–30% band that succulent roots tolerate.
citations: Gemini-report:Substrate Component Analysis and Transition to Peat-Free Media

shortDescription: All-mineral mix for the most water-sensitive cacti and mesembs (declared for schema; no v1 species mapped).
rationaleTemplate: A pure-mineral mix suits {species}: the absence of organic fines eliminates the slow-decomposition water-retention that demanding cacti and lithops cannot tolerate. This archetype is declared so the schema is exercised; no v1 species currently maps to it.

shortDescription: Coarse bark-dominant medium for velamen-rooted epiphytic orchids.

recipe.notes: Keeps the mix sweet; long-term structural porosity.
Drainage and aeration between bark pieces.

rationaleTemplate: A bark-dominant epiphytic mix suits {species}: velamen-coated aerial roots are evolved to absorb moisture quickly from rain, then dry within hours — coarse bark with charcoal and perlite reproduces the wet-then-dry rhythm an orchid's tree-branch habitat provides.

shortDescription: Coir-led mix with sphagnum for terrestrials that punish dry-back.

recipe.notes: Prevents waterlogging despite the high water-holding base.

rationaleTemplate: A moisture-retentive mix suits {species}: this terrestrial wants even, slightly above-standard humidity at the root zone, so a coir-led base with sphagnum gives the buffering capacity that prevents the rapid swings dry-back-intolerant taxa react badly to.

shortDescription: All-LECA passive-hydroponic substrate; requires hydroponic fertiliser.

recipe.notes: Inert; wicks water by capillary action from a reservoir.

rationaleTemplate: An all-LECA semi-hydro setup suits {species}: the aggregate is chemically inert, so a complete hydroponic fertiliser is mandatory — without it the plant will starve regardless of how well the wicking reservoir is managed. This archetype is declared so the schema and recommendation engine support the future semi-hydro lane; no v1 species currently maps to it.

shortDescription: Low-pH, bark-amended mix for calcifuges like Saintpaulia.

recipe.ingredient: Acidic coir or peat-free ericaceous base

recipe.notes: Drainage; avoids root rot risk at high water-holding.

recipe.ingredient: Acidic amendment (composted pine needles or sulphur)
recipe.notes: Keeps the substrate inside the ericaceous pH band over time.

rationaleTemplate: An ericaceous acidic mix suits {species}: micronutrient availability collapses above pH 6.5 for calcifuges, so the recipe targets pH 4.5–5.5 with bark fines and an acidic amendment to defend that band against creeping calcareous water and fertiliser drift.

shortDescription: Nutrient-poor peat/sand mix for temperate carnivores; zero fertiliser, zero lime, distilled/rain water only.

recipe.notes: Acidic, nutrient-poor organic base; the bog-soil analogue carnivores evolved in.
Inert drainage; must be lime-free (silica sand, not builder's/beach sand).

rationaleTemplate: A nutrient-poor peat/sand bog mix suits {species}: carnivorous plants evolved in mineral-starved acidic bogs and trap insects precisely because the substrate cannot feed them — so the mix carries NO fertiliser and NO lime/dolomite, and only distilled, reverse-osmosis, or rainwater is safe (tap-water minerals accumulate to toxic levels). A 50/50 sphagnum peat and lime-free silica sand blend reproduces that low-fertility, free-draining-yet-damp bog substrate.
citations: Drafter-sourced general horticulture (carnivorous plant cultivation; peat/sand bog mix, distilled-water mandate)
